summary: An 80-ft steel tower moved to Escoheag Hill and rebuilt by 1938; inactive since about 1990 and its wooden cab burned by vandals after 2009.

facts.status_note: Not an active lookout since about 1990; non-standard wooden cab burned by vandals sometime after 2009, destroying most upper landings and damaging the stairs. Burn marks and charred boards remain.
facts.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management

events.note: Originally erected on an unnamed knoll in the George Washington State Forest, Burrillville, per NHLR; a separate CCC history (Valley Breeze) names the structure the 'George Washington Memorial Fire Tower' in Glocester instead, and does not tie a build year to this tower specifically, though it notes the GW camp built three fire towers in 1935 generally -- so the two sources disagree on the town and arguably on the year
Moved from its original George Washington forest site
Reconstructed at the present Escoheag Hill site; the Former Fire Lookout Sites register independently gives the same year and credits the CCC

March 1952: a stove, electric generator, telephone and other equipment were stolen, and a map table was thrown from a window and damaged, per a fire-tower history site summarizing a contemporary newspaper account. Not in data/vocab.json event list, so recorded here as a note rather than a typed event.
Approximate; NHLR says the tower has not been an active lookout since around 1990
Wooden cab (a non-standard replacement) burned by vandals sometime after this year; exact year not given. Destroyed most upper landings and damaged the stairs

corrections.current: Story draft placed the tower "in the Arcadia Management Area of Kent County"
corrections.proposed: Drop the Arcadia Management Area claim; NHLR (source 1) only gives "Kent County, Rhode Island" and never mentions Arcadia
corrections.evidence: NHLR cached page text has no mention of Arcadia Management Area anywhere; the claim was unsupported by its cited footnote

sources.title: Across northern R.I. are signs of the Civilian Conservation Corps

notes_for_editor: Two loose ends worth a human look: (1) sources disagree on the tower's originating town before its 1937 move -- NHLR says Burrillville, the Valley Breeze CCC piece says Glocester -- and the Valley Breeze piece also states the tower was moved to 'Escoheag Hill in Exeter,' which would make Exeter the destination town rather than West Greenwich; that conflicts with NHLR's own location field of 'Kent County' (Exeter is in Washington County, West Greenwich in Kent County), so the destination town is unresolved and may itself be a second cross-source conflict, not just the origin town. The two sources may also disagree on build year: Valley Breeze gives 1935 as when the GW camp's three towers went up generally, versus NHLR's 1934, though Valley Breeze never ties that year to this specific tower by name. (2) The Former Fire Lookout Sites register carries a distinct, separate-looking listing, 'Escoheag Tower Site' (US 1585, RI 12), with coordinates about 0.4 miles from this tower's NHLR coordinates, but matching elevation, build year and agency -- almost certainly the same physical structure catalogued in both sister registers rather than a second nearby tower, but worth confirming. The 1952 burglary detail rests on a hobbyist site's paraphrase of an unnamed contemporary newspaper (identified there as the Newport Mercury, March 21 1952), not the original clipping, so it's included but flagged as the weakest-sourced fact here. Fact-check pass 2026-10-04 also found and removed an unsupported claim in the story draft that placed the tower 'in the Arcadia Management Area' -- the cited NHLR page never says this; see corrections.
